name: PAD Open Lower Extremity Revascularization (AFS Descriptive)
remarks: REUSE NOTE (pad-oler-amp-desc, 2026-06-13; amputation outcome added 2026-06-13):
Derived from pad-oler-macce-val/synthea/modules/pad_macce.json. It generates the
same OLER index procedures, preoperative comorbidities, procedure subtypes, and
laboratory values that back this study's Table 1 covariates
(covariates/covariates.csv groups 3-5).
The five MACCE outcome branch points from the source module have been REMOVED and
replaced with the amp-desc primary endpoint: a post-discharge major amputation
(above-knee or below-knee) in 50% of open-surgery patients, occurring 1 month to
5 years after the index OLER procedure. Amputations are emitted as
procedure_occurrence rows that map through concept_ancestor to the major_amputation
outcome cohort (cohort_id 2); those within the 180-day window populate the 6-month
AFS-loss stratum in Table 1, while later ones are AFS-intact at 6 months. All-cause
mortality (cohort 3) still arises only from Synthea's background-mortality module.
Original pad_macce.json remarks follow (outcome sections updated for amp-desc):
Models the full clinical pathway for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) from initial
diagnosis through treatment strategy selection, and — for patients who receive open
lower extremity revascularization — through the 30-day MACCE outcome window.
This module was derived from pad_ssi.json by replacing the SSI preoperative
comorbidity block with the 25 model-derived preoperative features from
covariates/covariate_concepts.csv (sourced from model/varImp.rds), and replacing
the SSI outcome states with the five MACCE components.
Clinical workflow:
1a. PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 20) years after age 60 (onset age 60-80)
1b. PAD diagnosis (ConditionOnset) — capped at age 90
2. Outpatient PAD diagnosis encounter
3. Document presenting symptom (asymptomatic, claudication, rest pain, wound/tissue loss)
4. Document preoperative features (cardiac conditions, antiplatelet/cardiac drugs,
and key laboratory measurements) derived from model covariate importance
5. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement
6. End outpatient encounter
7. Treatment strategy decision:
- Medical management (10%) → Terminal
- Endovascular revascularization (10%) → Terminal
- Open surgical revascularization (80%) → amputation outcome pathway
8. Pre-surgical workup delay (1-6 months)
9. Urgency flag (25% urgent/emergent)
10. Inpatient surgical admission → perioperative cefazolin → open revascularization
11. Post-operative inpatient stay (3-7 days) → discharge
12. Post-discharge amputation gate (50%) → AKA/BKA after a 1mo-5yr delay; else Terminal
Cohort definitions:
Target  : inpatient surgery for open lower extremity revascularization
Outcome : major amputation (AKA/BKA); 6-month amputation-free survival is the
primary descriptive endpoint (composite of amputation + all-cause death)
Amputation outcome assumptions:
Major amputation incidence after open surgery : 50%
Amputation type split                         : 50% above-knee (AKA), 50% below-knee (BKA)
Time from index OLER to amputation            : Uniform(1 month, 5 years)
Simons et al. 2016 novel VQI AFS prognostic-model covariates (Group 6 of
covariates/covariates.csv), generated 2026-06-15:
dialysisDependent  : 12% — hemodialysis procedure (SNOMED 302497006 -> OMOP 4120120)
functionalDependent: 20% — impaired mobility (SNOMED 82971005 -> OMOP 4306934, Observation)
prostheticConduit  : per-anatomy prosthetic-graft co-code on the index bypass
EA 95% 405309005; endarterectomy = none)
antiplatelet/weight: already generated (aspirin/clopidogrel orders; Synthea core vitals)
Preoperative covariate prevalence assumptions (from model/varImp.rds, covariates/covariates.csv):

Timing:

Inpatient stay            : 3-7 days post-surgery
Amputation timing         : 1 month - 5 years after the index OLER procedure
Usage:
Copy to <synthea_home>/src/main/resources/modules/ and run Synthea normally.
To load into the omop_synth database, run this project's Step 5 CSV-to-OMOP ETL workflow.
Does NOT model: graft failure, reintervention, or non-amputation limb events; all-cause
mortality arises only from Synthea's background-mortality module (not surgery-linked).
PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 5) years after age 60 (onset age 60-65).
Shortened from the original 0-20 yr window (onset 60-80) to MAXIMIZE PAD
incidence: with onset occurring soon after the age-60 guard, essentially
every patient who survives to 60 develops PAD (and thus becomes eligible
for the OLER target cohort), rather than losing a large fraction to
mortality across a 20-year onset window. PAD remains 100% incident
conditional on reaching age 60 -- there is no probabilistic PAD gate.
Trade-off: the index-age distribution is compressed toward 60-66, so the
Table 1 age_group rows skew to <65 (the >=75 bucket nearly empties).
Widen this range to restore age spread at the cost of fewer cases.
Age_90_Check still guards against procedures on patients over age 90.
Cap the PAD pathway at age 90. Patients older than 90 after the
onset delay are routed to Terminal so procedure ages stay realistic.
Initial outpatient PAD evaluation encounter.
Presenting symptom, preoperative comorbidities, and ABI documented here.
Documents presenting symptom / Rutherford class at first evaluation.
Rutherford 0: asymptomatic (10%)
Rutherford 1-3: claudication (50%)
Rutherford 4: rest pain (25%)
Rutherford 5-6: wound / tissue loss (15%)

codes.display: Neutrophils/100 leukocytes in Blood by Automated count

remarks: Neutrophil percentage — CBC differential (OMOP concept 3012608).
Normal range: 45-75%. Elevated values reflect systemic inflammation.
LOINC 770-8 maps to OMOP concept 3012608 (Measurement domain).
Serum creatinine — renal function marker (OMOP concept 3016723).
Normal: 0.6-1.2 mg/dL. Elevated in CKD, common comorbidity in PAD.
LOINC 2160-0 maps to OMOP concept 3016723 (Measurement domain).
Hemoglobin — anemia marker (OMOP concept 3000963).
Normal: 12.0-17.5 g/dL. Anemia is common in PAD and increases MACCE risk.
LOINC 718-7 maps to OMOP concept 3000963 (Measurement domain).
Total cholesterol (OMOP concept 3027114).
Range: 140-280 mg/dL in this PAD population on variable lipid therapy.
LOINC 2093-3 maps to OMOP concept 3027114 (Measurement domain).

Treatment decision following PAD evaluation.
Oversampled for open surgical revascularization (OLER) — the study target
cohort — to maximize the number of characterizable index cases. Only the
open-surgical branch enters the target cohort; medical and endovascular
patients exit the module and are not characterized.
Medical management (5%): antiplatelet, statin, exercise therapy — no procedure.
Endovascular (5%): balloon angioplasty / stenting — not an open surgery, exits pathway.
Open surgical (90%): open lower extremity revascularization — proceeds to the
amputation outcome pathway.
Patient managed with medical therapy only.
No revascularization — exits the module.

SNOMED-CT 73994005 routes to OMOP procedure_occurrence via concept 4158569.

Standard inpatient stay after open lower extremity bypass: 3-7 days.
Discharge from the index OLER surgical admission. Patients then enter the
post-discharge major amputation gate (the study's primary endpoint).
Post-discharge major amputation — the amp-desc primary endpoint component.
50% of open-surgery patients undergo a major lower-extremity amputation
(AKA or BKA) during follow-up; the remaining 50% stay amputation-free and
transition to Terminal. The amputation-free survival (AFS) analysis in
workflow/08 counts an amputation as 6-month AFS loss only when it falls
within the 180-day prediction window after the index OLER procedure.
Time from the index OLER procedure to major amputation: 1 month to 5 years,
uniformly distributed (per study design). Amputations within 180 days of the
index procedure populate the 6-month AFS-loss stratum in Table 1; later
amputations are AFS-intact at 6 months but are still captured by the
major_amputation outcome cohort (cohort_id 2).
Inpatient admission for the major amputation procedure.
Split major amputations evenly between above-knee (AKA) and below-knee (BKA).
Both SNOMED procedure codes map through concept_ancestor to the
major_amputation outcome cohort (study_params.yaml ancestor_concept_ids
include 4195136 = AKA and 4338257 = BKA).
Above-knee amputation (AKA).
SNOMED 79733001 -> OMOP concept 4195136 [vocab query] (Procedure, standard).
4195136 is itself a major_amputation ancestor, so the outcome cohort's
concept_ancestor rollup captures this procedure_occurrence row.
